players.note: Tetairoa McMillan is the WR13 in fantasy points per game. In the four games he has played with Jalen Coker as a full-time player, McMillan has had a 21.5% target share with 2.19 YPRR, four red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 27.9% first-read share. This week McMillan faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four games with Coker as a full-go, McMillan has had a 21% TPRR and 2.67 YPRR against two high. McMillan has a nice shot at a bounce-back game this week against a Green Bay secondary that (since Week 3) has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

George Pickens is the WR24 in fantasy points per game with at least 15 PPR points in two of his last three games. I'm projecting a milder stat line this week for Pickens. Yes, you guessed it. Arizona is a two-high, heavy pass defense. Pickens has a 20.5% target share with 2.00 YPRR, six red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 23.1% first-read share. Arizona has the highest two-high rate in the NFL (70.5%). Against two high, Pickens' TPRR drops off a map from 35% (against single high) to 17%, and his YPRR falls from 2.92 to 1.51. Working in his favor is the fact that Arizona has been horrible at defending perimeter wide receivers, which could help counteract Pickens' coverage woes. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Pickens could still be a decent WR2 this week, but this doesn't look like a blow-up spot.

Garrett Wilson is the WR22 in fantasy points per game, but he has had fewer than nine PPR points in three of his last four games. With that said, Wilson could get the squeaky wheel treatment this week. Overall, Wilson still has a 25.1% target share with 2.09 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 30.6% first-read share. His quiet Week 6 performance is easily explainable, as he had to deal with Christian Gonzalez on 93.9% of his routes. The Raiders don't have a corner in that talent area code on their depth chart. In their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the fifth-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Jalen Coker didn't have the massive game last week that I was projecting, as Carolina's passing offense cratered as Bryce Young fell back to Earth. Coker could have a bounce-back outing this week. In his four full games this season, Coker has had a 22.2% target share with 2.40 YPRR, five red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 30.2% first-read share. Overall, he is the WR22 in fantasy points per game. This week, Coker faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four full games, against two-high, Coker has had a 23% TPRR with 1.85 YPRR. Bryce Young will have to look like his early-season form for this passing attack to have bite again, but it's possible. Since Week 3, Green Bay has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

Michael Wilson has been struggling recently. Wilson is still the WR32 in fantasy points per game, but he hasn't managed more than 12 PPR points since Marvin Harrison Jr.'s departure from Arizona. Since Week 5, he has had a 16% target share with 1.01 YPRR, three red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 17.8% first-read share. He hasn't finished with more than 55 receiving yards in any of these three games. I think he can break out of his funk this week. Dallas has the third-highest single-high rate in the NFL (71.1%). Wilson has crushed single-high this season with a 31% TPRR and 2.03 YPRR. Joey Porter Jr. hasn't been shadowing in Dallas, so I don't expect him to this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

DJ Moore (shoulder) practiced on a limited basis all week. He has been listed as questionable, but he is expected to play this week. In his two full games this season, Moore has had a 30.9% target share, 3.63 YPRR, 0.174 FD/RR, and a 33.3% first-read share. In those two contests, he racked up two red zone targets and four deep targets. No matter how you slice it, that's elite usage for a wide receiver. Moore is a strong WR2 this week with WR1 upside. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the third-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Luther Burden is the WR24 in fantasy points per game and looks electric any time he touches the ball. Luther Burden's route share dipped to 41.5% in Week 6, but he was back up at 66.7% last week. Overall, Burden has a 19.5% target share, 2.70 YPRR, nine red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. This week, he'll face a Seattle pass defense that has the seventh-highest two-high rate in the NFL (60.2%). Against two-high, Burden has a 25% TPRR and 3.07 YPRR. Those numbers are incredibly strong. Burden has a nasty matchup this week, but he also has the talent to walk away with a solid stat line this week despite it. Across their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Stefon Diggs will be leading the way for Washington's aerial attack moving forward. Diggs is the WR24 in fantasy points per game with a 20.9% target share, 1.60 YPRR, five red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 25.4% first-read share. Diggs should be a strong WR2 this week. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the 13th-most yards per target, the most receiving fantasy points per game, and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Every time I think DK Metcalf should smash, he turns in a wet fart stat line. Metcalf started hot with 56 receiving yards in the first half last week before falling asleep after halftime. Metcalf is the WR36 in fantasy points per game, with four games this season with fewer than nine PPR points. Metcalf has a 21.9% target share with 1.41 YPRR, four red zone targets, 14 deep targets, and a 31.7% first-read share. This week, he faces a Browns pass defense that has the highest single high rate in the NFL (75.2%). Against single high, Metcalf's TPRR has risen from 20% to 23%, and his YPRR has increased from 1.11 to 1.56. The coverage structure is in his favor, but Cleveland has been shutting down perimeter wide receivers. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 5, Germie Bernard has been the WR23 in fantasy points per game with a 22.7% target share, 1.92 YPRR (4.8 aDOT), four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 21.4% first-read share. He has essentially been Pittsburgh's Rashee Rice with a 24% designed target share. This week, he faces a Browns pass defense that has the highest single high rate in the NFL (75.2%). Against single high, since Week 5, Bernard has had a 19% TPRR and 2.05 YPRR. Bernard has a solid matchup this week and could have a bounce-back game after a quiet outing against the Saints. Across their last five games, the Browns have allowed the 12th-most yards per target to slot receivers while ranking 19th in fantasy points per opportunity.

Hello, Omar Cooper Jr. I'm sorry for doubting you last week. Over the last two games, Cooper has been the WR6 and WR9 in weekly scoring. In those games, Cooper had a 20% target share, 4.45 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 29.3% first-read share. Cooper could have another fantastic game in Week 8. In their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the fourth-most receiving fantasy points per game, the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity, and the most receiving touchdowns (tied) to slot receivers.

Well, I hoped KC Concepcion would have his breakout game last week, and it happened. Concepcion was the WR8 in weekly scoring. That pulls him up to WR51 in fantasy points per game for the season. I know, not great. He has a 20.5% target share with 1.73 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 27.1% first-read share. It's possible Concepcion keeps the train rolling this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 11th-most fantasy points per game to slot receivers.

Ok, Jamo...I'm sorry. I was down on Jamo last week, and he made me pay for it. Jameson Williams is the WR25 in fantasy points per game after the big game. Williams has a 16.6% target share with 1.75 YPRR, seven red zone targets, ten deep targets (eighth among wideouts), and a 23.4% first-read share. After last week, Williams' numbers against two high look much better, which will help him this week. Minnesota has the fourth-highest two-high rate (63.3%). Against two-high, Williams has a 19% TPRR (second on the team) and 1.81 YPRR. Jared Goff will be blitzed into oblivion this week, and Williams should be a trusted weapon on those plays. Williams has a 19% TPRR and 2.04 when Goff has been blitzed. It's a tough matchup for Williams, so consider him a volatile player this week as usual. Over their last five games, Minny has allowed the third-fewest yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Wan'Dale Robinson is the WR54 in fantasy points per game with three outings this season with at least 11 PPR points. With Carnell Tate out, Robinson will operate as Tennessee's WR1. He's in a great spot to capitalize on the bump in role this week. DJ Turner isn't moving to nickel full time, so Robinson should have a nice matchup. Robinson has a 20.2% target share with 1.15 YPRR, eight red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 25.9% first-read share. His FD/RR is a solid 0.084. Cincy has been bleeding out production to slot receivers. Across their last five games, Cincy has allowed the fifth-most yards per target, the most fantasy points per opportunity, and the most receiving touchdowns (tied) to slot receivers.

Well, damn. Ok, I guess it's time to start believing in Tre Tucker. Tucker has three weeks with at least 21 PPR points this season as the WR20 in fantasy points per game. Tucker has a 17.7% target share with 2.18 YPRR, six red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 23.3% first-read share. Tucker could keep the party bus rolling in Week 8. In their last five games, the Jets have allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Denzel Boston has dropped to the WR34 after two quiet weeks. Over the last two games, he has scored only 8.2 PPR points combined. Overall, he has a 19% target share with 1.68 YPRR, five red zone targets, 14 deep targets, and a 22.9% first-read share. Unfortunately, it looks like Boston is headed toward another quieter day. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity against the position.

It looks like Ladd McConkey will be back this week after sustaining a concussion in Week 6. McConkey has been in and out of the lineup all season with the concussion, a rib issue, a foot issue, and a chest injury. When he has been on the field, he has had a 20% TPRR, 2.22 YPRR, and a 14.1% first-read share. It's tough to consider him as anything more than a dart-throw flex at this point in the season with a bad matchup. Over their last five games, the Rams have allowed the second-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Well, it happened. Makai Lemon had his best game of the season against a horrible Dallas secondary. Lemon was the WR13 for the week. Over the last two weeks, Lemon has had a 16.3% target share with 1.13 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 21.4% first-read share. Lemon offers some flex upside this week with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks out. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers while ranking 16th in yards per target allowed to the position.

Keenan Allen has been producing. Across his last four games, Allen has finished as the WR20, WR35, WR17, and WR44 in weekly scoring. Since Week 3, he has led the team with a 22.2% target share and 25.7% first-read share while posting 1.94 YPRR with three red zone targets and two deep targets. Allen could be a strong flex again this week. Across their last five games, the Jags have given up the fourth-most yards per target and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Chris Godwin hasn't been fantasy relevant all year as the WR64 in fantasy points per game. He has yet to post even double-digit PPR points. Godwin has a 16.6% target share, 1.18 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 19.3% first-read share. It's been tough to watch. Godwin is a sit-and-droppable at this point. Across their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Well, I was all in on Malik Washington, and he had arguably his worst game of the season. Overall, Washington is the WR42 in fantasy points per game. Last week, with Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas active, Washington ran 60% of his routes from the slot. Overall, Washington has had a 25.8% target share with 1.85 YPRR, two red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 28.1% first-read share. Since Week 6, New England has had the third-highest single-high rate (66.7%). This season, against single high, Washington has had a 22% TPRR and 1.85 YPRR. Washington could have a bounce-back game this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the third-most yards per target and the second-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Jaylen Waddle opened this week (chest) with a DNP. He managed limited practice sessions on Thursday and Friday. He has been listed as questionable. I could easily see him being ruled out Sunday before kickoff, so monitor the news all day and be prepared with a backup option if you're looking to start him. I'm leaning toward sitting him this week, even if he is active, though. Waddle has been crushed by Bo Nix before this injury occurred. He is the WR48 in fantasy points per game. Waddle has a 19.7% target share with 1.56 YPRR, three red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 29% first-read share. He has a horrible matchup this week. Across their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Jordan Addison has been almost non-existent this season, as the WR65 in fantasy points per game. Addison has a 17.9% target share with 1.25 YPRR, one red zone target, five deep targets, and a 24.1% first-read share. Addison has failed to surpass 60 receiving yards in all but one game this season. Addison could double that output after this week. Detroit has the eighth-highest rate of single-high (56.9%). Against single-high, Addison's usage has gone up, with this TPRR rising from 12% to 21% and his YPRR jumping from 0.78 (against two-high) to 1.77. Now, Detroit has tightened up its defense against perimeter receivers over the last five games, allowing the 11th-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity, which leaves Addison as a middle-of-the-road flex.

Last week, DeMario Douglas was a popular flex that burned people. Well, it's time to go back to the well this week. Since Week 5, Douglas has had a 17.5% target share, a 65.1% route share, 2.45 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 16.1% first-read share. Since Week 2, Miami has had the ninth-highest two-high rate (56.6%). Since Week 5, against two-high, Douglas has had a 22% TPRR and 2.86 YPRR. Over their last five games, Miami has faced the second-fewest slot targets while allowing the sixth-most yards per target to position. Douglas is a strong flex this week.

Jakobi Meyers is the WR37 in fantasy points per game with three top-36 weekly finishes (WR28, WR17, WR27). Meyers has a 15.2% target share with 1.85 YPRR, six red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 17.3% first-read share. He has quietly taken a step back and become the third option in the passing game this season behind Parker Washington and Brenton Strange. This week, he could easily post a strong flex-worthy stat line. Indy has the 12th-highest single-high rate (52.1%). Against single-high, Meyers has a 17% TPRR and 2.02 YPRR. Meyers could succeed this week, but it's not an easy matchup. Across their last five games, Indy has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the ninth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Meyers is dealing with ankle and hamstring issues. He practiced on a limited basis before missing Friday's practice. He has been listed as questionable. I hate late week downgrades. Monitor the news. I could see Meyers getting ruled out this weekend.

Josh Downs has been slumping. I'm not laying this at the feet of Downs. It's a Daniel Jones problem. Downs hasn't had more than 50 receiving yards in a game since Week 3. Over the last four games, Downs hasn't finished higher than WR41 in any game. Since Week 4, Downs has had a 13.4% target share with 0.86 YPRR, one red zone target, four deep targets, and a 17% first-read share. Indy would be wise to feature him this week to drive his trade stock up, but we'll see if that happens. Downs is flex-viable again this week. In their last five games, Jacksonville has allowed the ninth-most yards per target to slot receivers while ranking 17th in fantasy points per opportunity.

Ryan Flournoy has replaced Jake Ferguson as the third wheel in the Dallas passing attack. Since Week 5, Flournoy has had a 13.8% target share, 1.96 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 12.2% first-read share. Arizona has the highest two-high rate in the NFL (70.5%). Since Week 5, against two-high, Flournoy has seen his TPRR increase from 14% to 18% while posting 1.78 YPRR. Flournoy is a solid flex option this week. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Khalil Shakir might be the WR45 in fantasy points per game, but in his last three games, he has had at least 11 PPR points in each game. In those three games, Shakir has had an 18.8% target share with 2.68 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 24.1% first-read share. Baltimore has the fifth-highest rate of two-high (62.4%). Against two-high, Shakir has a 21% TPRR and 2.07 YPRR. Shakir is a strong flex this week against a Baltimore pass defense that, across their last five games, has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers. DJ Moore's return could hinder Shakir's ceiling this week, but he should still return a nice stat line.

Rashee Rice will be back this week (hamstring). He opened the week with limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. He had a full practice on Friday. Rice doesn't carry an injury designation into this week. In Weeks 1-3, Rice was the WR23 in fantasy points per game. He had a 16.3% target share with 2.35 YPRR, four red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 20.3% first-read share. Rice will have a long day this week. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the 14th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. They will also get Patrick Surtain back. If you're forced to start Rice, I get it, but temper your expectations this week.

While I think Luther Burden can overcome a horrible matchup, I don't share the same optimism for Rome Odunze this week. Odunze is the WR55 in fantasy points per game with a 15.4% target share with 1.70 YPRR, five red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 17.6% first-read share. Across their last five games, Seattle has allowed the tenth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game and the 14th-fewest yards per target to perimeter wide receivers. Sit Odunze this week.

Xavier Worthy is having another forgettable season as the WR53 in fantasy points per game. He has scored at least 11 PPR points this season only three times. Worthy has an 18.3% target share with 1.25 YPRR, four red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 25.6% first-read share. Worthy is a sit again this week. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity while ranking 15th in receiving fantasy points per game against perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, in his return to the lineup, Caleb Douglas secured two of his three targets with 70 receiving yards and two scores. Douglas had a 67.9% route share, a 14.3% target share, one red zone target, and a 16.7% first-read share. Christian Gonzalez could shadow either Caleb Douglas this week. It's also possible that doesn't happen. Last week, Gonzalez only followed Rome Odunze on 40.5% of his routes. Since Week 6, New England has had the third-highest single high rate (66.7%). This season, against single high, Douglas has had a 20% TPRR with 1.96 YPRR. If Douglas doesn't get shadowed by Christian Gonzalez this week, he could have another strong showing. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Dallas has been BLEEDING out production to the slot all season. Kendrick Bourne could be the next slot receiver to eat them alive this week. Since Week 5, Bourne has had one game with at least 12 PPR points while seeing a 15.3% target share with 1.45 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 16.7% first-read share. In their last five games, Dallas has allowed the most yards per target, the most receiving yards, and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers. Makai Lemon was the WR13 in weekly scoring last week against this defense.

Courtland Sutton's fantasy value is non-existent. He is the WR70 in fantasy points per game without one game with at least double-digit PPR points. Sutton has a 14.2% target share with 0.94 YPRR, seven red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 21% first-read share. Sutton is a sit again this week. Across their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, Ja'Kobi Lane was second on the team with a 14.7% target share while having a 65% route share. Lane finished with 25 receiving yards (0.96 YPRR), two red zone targets, and a 15.4% first-read share (second on the team). Lane is a viable flex option this week. Over the last five weeks, Buffalo has allowed the second-most receiving fantasy points per game and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.
Tre Harris opened this week with a limited practice (hamstring). I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Last week, in his first game back from the finger injury, Adonai Mitchell had only a 51.5% route share, a 10% target share, and a 15% first-read share. He's a sit this week and until further notice, until we see his playing time jump back into a full-time starting workload. That could be this week, but it's impossible to know and not worth the risk in Week 8.

Last week, Chris Bell had only a 53.6% route share and 48.4% snap rate with Caleb Douglas back and Malik Washington in the lineup. We need to see Chris Bell's usage bounce back with Douglas back in the lineup before putting him into a fantasy lineup.

Brian Thomas Jr.'s only hope this season seems to be a trade at this point. Over the last two games, he has played only 51.4% and 21.1% of the snaps while drawing a total of five targets (zero receptions). He's not startable for fantasy purposes until something changes.
